rule_text: Pair a dark two-piece business suit with black cap-toe or plain-toe oxford shoes for the highest level of daytime business formality.
evidence_keywords: suit, oxford, black shoes, business formal, cap-toe
source_title: Dressing the Man: Mastering the Art of Permanent Fashion
source_reliability_reason: Book by an authoritative menswear author widely cited as a reference on classic tailored dressing.
evidence_basis: Flusser presents the oxford as the most formal daytime shoe and pairs black oxfords with dark business suits.
rule_scope: Applies to classic business or formal daytime dress codes in menswear.
rule_limitations: May not apply to fashion-forward suits, unstructured suits, or intentionally casual pairings.
notes: Use as a strong evidence anchor for formal menswear shoe recommendations.

rule_text: With a navy or charcoal suit worn in less strictly formal business contexts a mid to dark brown oxford or derby is an acceptable alternative to black.
evidence_keywords: navy suit, brown shoes, derby, business
source_title: Gentleman: A Timeless Guide to Fashion
source_reliability_reason: Comprehensive reference volume by an author widely cited for classic menswear conventions.
evidence_basis: Roetzel describes brown shoes as acceptable with navy or grey suits outside the strictest business formal contexts.
rule_scope: Applies to modern business and business-casual menswear.
rule_limitations: May be inappropriate for the most conservative formal contexts (e.g. traditional legal or diplomatic dress).
notes: Useful counter-rule to R001 for softer business contexts.

rule_text: Match the leather colour of your shoes to the leather colour of your belt so the two accessories read as one coordinated leather statement.
evidence_keywords: belt, shoes, leather, matching, colour coordination
source_title: Dressing the Man: Mastering the Art of Permanent Fashion
source_reliability_reason: Book is a widely cited reference on classic tailored dressing principles.
evidence_basis: Flusser articulates the shoe-and-belt colour match as a foundational rule of classic dressing.
rule_scope: Applies to classic tailored and smart-casual dress with visible leather belt and leather shoes.
rule_limitations: May not apply where the belt is deliberately contrasting as a design accent, or where no belt is worn.
notes: Use as a paired coordination rule with any shoe recommendation involving a visible belt.

rule_text: For smart-casual menswear a penny loafer or tassel loafer in polished leather provides a step down from the oxford while retaining tailored formality.
evidence_keywords: loafer, penny loafer, smart casual, chinos, blazer
source_title: True Style: The History and Principles of Classic Menswear
source_reliability_reason: Book by a menswear historian and long-time editor published by a respected trade press.
evidence_basis: Boyer traces the loafer's evolution from casual footwear to an accepted smart-casual staple in modern tailoring.
rule_scope: Applies to blazer-and-trouser or chino-based smart-casual menswear.
rule_limitations: Not appropriate for strict business-formal or black-tie occasions.
notes: Anchor rule for smart-casual shoe pairings in menswear evidence chains.

rule_text: A clean minimal white leather sneaker functions as a neutral base that can be worn with jeans chinos or unstructured tailoring for a casual-to-smart-casual look.
evidence_keywords: white sneaker, minimal, jeans, chinos, casual
source_title: Style Journal
source_reliability_reason: Established luxury retailer with an editorially curated journal.
evidence_basis: Mr Porter's style features repeatedly identify the minimal white sneaker as a wardrobe neutral suitable for smart-casual dressing.
rule_scope: Applies to casual and smart-casual outfits built on jeans chinos or soft tailoring.
rule_limitations: Not appropriate for formal or business-formal dress codes.
notes: Verify specific journal article URL when finalising bibliography.

rule_text: A fine-gauge turtleneck under a tailored blazer provides a warmer alternative to a shirt-and-tie combination and reads as elevated smart-casual.

rule_scope: Applies to womenswear proportion balancing.

evidence_basis: Vogue workwear features consistently pair silk shells with tailored jackets in warm weather.

rule_text: A denim shirt reads as more casual than a cotton dress shirt and layers well over a plain t-shirt or under an unstructured jacket.

rule_scope: Applies to casual and smart-casual layered outfits.

rule_text: A fitted cotton t-shirt is the base casual top that layers under jackets shirts and knitwear across dress codes from casual to smart-casual.

evidence_basis: Boyer treats the plain t-shirt as a fundamental modern casual base layer.

rule_text: Contrasting top and bottom colours emphasise the waist by creating a visual break at the hemline while tonal top and bottom colours elongate the silhouette.

evidence_basis: Roetzel articulates contrast at the waist as a silhouette-shaping colour device.

evidence_keywords: dress shirt, collar, cuff, tie, formal

evidence_basis: Flusser distinguishes formal from casual shirts by collar and cuff construction.

rule_text: A straight-leg trouser is a versatile silhouette that works across smart-casual and business dress codes because it neither exaggerates nor minimises the leg line.
evidence_keywords: straight leg, trouser, versatile, tailored
source_title: Dressing the Man: Mastering the Art of Permanent Fashion
evidence_basis: Flusser identifies the straight leg as a neutral versatile trouser cut.
rule_scope: Applies to menswear and by extension to general tailored dressing.

rule_text: Trouser hem length should sit close to the top of the shoe with only a slight break in formal contexts and a shorter cropped break in modern smart-casual contexts.
evidence_keywords: trouser break, hem length, shoe, tailoring
source_title: True Style: The History and Principles of Classic Menswear
evidence_basis: Boyer describes the shoe-adjacent trouser break as classic and shorter breaks as modern.
rule_scope: Applies to tailored menswear trouser hem.
rule_limitations: Not applicable to jeans or casual trousers.

rule_text: Dark indigo denim reads as more formal than lighter washes and can be worn as a smart-casual trouser alternative with a blazer or jacket.
evidence_keywords: dark denim, indigo, blazer, smart casual
source_title: Style Journal
evidence_basis: Mr Porter journal features consistently rank dark indigo denim above lighter washes in the smart-casual hierarchy.

rule_text: Light-wash and distressed denim is stronger in casual daytime contexts and weaker in workwear or smart-casual contexts because the finish signals informality.
evidence_keywords: light wash denim, distressed, casual, daytime
source_title: GQ

rule_scope: Applies to casual daytime dressing.
rule_limitations: Not appropriate for workwear or formal contexts.

source_title: Vogue
evidence_basis: Vogue silhouette features pair wide trousers with fitted tops.
rule_scope: Applies to smart-casual and evening silhouette-balancing outfits.
rule_limitations: Not appropriate where a straight column silhouette is intended.

rule_text: A cigarette or slim ankle-length trouser pairs cleanly with a heeled shoe by exposing the ankle and drawing the eye down to the shoe.
evidence_keywords: cigarette trouser, ankle length, heel, workwear
source_title: The Little Black Book of Style
evidence_basis: Garcia pairs cigarette trousers with heeled shoes for workwear silhouette.

evidence_keywords: pleated trouser, drape, full cut, tailored
source_title: Dressing the Man: Mastering the Art of Permanent Fashion
evidence_basis: Flusser discusses pleats as a drape feature that requires a fuller trouser cut.

rule_limitations: Not appropriate for slim modern silhouettes.

evidence_keywords: flat front, slim trouser, modern, tailored
source_title: True Style: The History and Principles of Classic Menswear
evidence_basis: Boyer identifies flat-front trousers as the modern lean silhouette.
rule_scope: Applies to modern tailored menswear.
rule_limitations: Not appropriate for classic wide pleated cuts.

rule_scope: Applies to womenswear workwear.

rule_limitations: Not appropriate for tailored formal dress codes.

rule_text: A tweed jacket carries country and heritage associations and pairs cleanly with wool trousers and knitwear in cool-weather smart-casual and countryside dressing.
evidence_keywords: tweed jacket, country, wool, cool weather
source_title: True Style: The History and Principles of Classic Menswear
evidence_basis: Boyer traces tweed to British country tradition and identifies its modern smart-casual role.
rule_scope: Applies to cool-weather smart-casual dressing.
rule_limitations: Not appropriate for warm-weather or formal city dressing.

rule_text: A shearling or teddy-fabric coat introduces textural volume to an outfit and is best paired with lean underlayers so the coat is the focal texture.
evidence_keywords: shearling, teddy, texture, focal, coat
source_title: Vogue
evidence_basis: Vogue features present shearling and teddy coats as focal-texture pieces.
rule_scope: Applies to casual and smart-casual winter dressing.
rule_limitations: Volume and heat may be limiting factors.

rule_text: A cardigan is a soft knit layer that reads as more casual than a blazer and can substitute as light outerwear in warm interiors.
evidence_keywords: cardigan, soft knit, layering, blazer alternative
source_title: Tim Gunn's Fashion Bible
evidence_basis: Gunn discusses cardigans as a soft blazer alternative for smart-casual dressing.
rule_scope: Applies to smart-casual dressing in mild conditions.
rule_limitations: Not appropriate as primary outdoor cold-weather coat.

rule_text: A bomber jacket has military flight-wear origins and is a casual to smart-casual layering piece well suited to lightweight cool-weather dressing.
evidence_keywords: bomber jacket, military, casual, smart casual
source_title: Uniform: Clothing and Discipline in the Modern World
source_author_or_org: Jane Tynan and Lisa Godson (eds.), Bloomsbury
source_reliability_reason: Academic edited volume on uniform history.
evidence_basis: The volume documents the military flight jacket origins of the modern bomber.
rule_scope: Applies to smart-casual and casual dressing.
rule_limitations: Not appropriate for formal business or tailored evening contexts.

rule_text: Formal daytime outerwear conventionally reaches at least the knee to preserve the tailored line of the suit or dress underneath.
evidence_keywords: coat length, knee, formal, tailored
source_title: Dressing the Man: Mastering the Art of Permanent Fashion
evidence_basis: Flusser prescribes at least knee-length coats for tailored formal dressing.
rule_scope: Applies to tailored formal outerwear.
rule_limitations: Not applicable to casual short jackets.

rule_text: A structured shoulder on outerwear signals formality because it echoes the tailored suit shoulder while an unstructured shoulder signals softness and informality.
evidence_keywords: structured shoulder, unstructured, formality, outerwear
source_title: Dressing the Man: Mastering the Art of Permanent Fashion
evidence_basis: Flusser identifies structured shoulders as a formal tailoring signal.
rule_scope: Applies to tailored menswear outerwear.
rule_limitations: Modern soft tailoring intentionally deconstructs the shoulder.

rule_text: An overcoat should cover the full length of the suit jacket including cuffs so no jacket fabric is visible below or beyond the overcoat sleeves and hem.
evidence_keywords: overcoat, sleeve length, hem length, suit jacket
source_title: True Style: The History and Principles of Classic Menswear
evidence_basis: Boyer prescribes full coverage of the suit jacket by the overcoat in classic proportions.
rule_scope: Applies to tailored menswear layering.
rule_limitations: Not applicable to short casual jackets.

rule_text: The formality of the outerwear should match the formality of the occasion so a wool overcoat suits a suit while a bomber jacket suits smart casual dressing.
evidence_keywords: outerwear formality, occasion matching, overcoat, bomber
source_title: Gentleman: A Timeless Guide to Fashion
evidence_basis: Roetzel maps outerwear categories to occasion formality.
rule_scope: Applies to outerwear selection across dress codes.
rule_limitations: Modern styling intentionally mixes categories for effect.

rule_text: A wool-blend coat provides a balance between warmth structure and drape making it a versatile mid-weight outerwear option across dress codes.
evidence_keywords: wool blend, mid weight, versatile, outerwear
source_title: Style Journal
evidence_basis: Mr Porter features consistently recommend wool-blend coats as versatile mid-weight outerwear.
rule_scope: Applies to cool-weather versatile dressing.
rule_limitations: Not appropriate for extreme cold or high-formality evening dress.

rule_text: With smart-casual white leather sneakers as the anchor, cropped or straight-leg trousers keep the sneaker visible while wider ankle-hiding cuts visually shorten the shoe.
evidence_keywords: white sneaker, cropped trouser, ankle, minimal
source_title: Style Journal
evidence_basis: Mr Porter journal repeatedly pairs minimal sneakers with cropped or straight-leg trousers as a proportion strategy.
rule_scope: Applies to smart-casual outfits anchored by a sneaker.
rule_limitations: Not appropriate for tailored formal contexts.
notes: Symmetric shoe-first pairing rule for R020.

rule_text: When formal oxford shoes are chosen for a business or formal occasion the trouser should be a wool worsted or crepe cut with a slight break to preserve the coordinated formality of the outfit.
evidence_keywords: oxford, wool trouser, worsted, break
source_title: Dressing the Man: Mastering the Art of Permanent Fashion
evidence_basis: Flusser links formal footwear to matching trouser fabric and cut in classic tailoring.
rule_scope: Applies to formal menswear with oxford shoes.
rule_limitations: Not appropriate for casual or knit trousers.
notes: Symmetric shoe-first pairing rule for R001.

rule_text: A statement necklace requires an unornamented crew or scoop neckline as its backing so the neckline does not compete with the focal accessory.
evidence_keywords: statement necklace, plain neckline, focal, backing
source_title: The Little Black Book of Style
source_reliability_reason: Editorial book by a former Elle fashion director.
evidence_basis: Garcia advises plain necklines to support statement necklaces so the accessory remains focal.
rule_scope: Applies to womenswear focal-necklace outfits.
rule_limitations: Not applicable to layered or subtle jewellery choices.
notes: Symmetric top-first pairing rule for R032.

rule_text: A dress watch on a fine leather strap is the appropriate wrist accessory when a tailored overcoat is worn over a suit so both watch and outerwear signal the same formal register.
evidence_keywords: dress watch, leather strap, overcoat, suit, formality
source_title: Gentleman: A Timeless Guide to Fashion
evidence_basis: Roetzel matches dress-watch formality to tailored outerwear.
rule_scope: Applies to formal menswear cool-weather layering.
rule_limitations: Not applicable to casual sport watches or casual outerwear.

rule_text: Wedding guests in Western conventions traditionally avoid solid white or ivory as the dominant top or dress colour so the bride remains visually distinct within the ceremony.
evidence_keywords: wedding guest, white, ivory, colour convention
source_title: Emily Posts Etiquette
source_author_or_org: Emily Post Institute (Peggy Post et al.)
source_url_or_reference: Emily Posts Etiquette (19th edition), William Morrow, 2017
source_reliability_reason: Long-established etiquette reference published by a recognised authority on social conventions.
evidence_basis: Emily Post etiquette codifies the convention that wedding guests avoid white or ivory.
rule_scope: Applies to Western wedding-guest occasions.
rule_limitations: Cultural and modern wedding practices may vary; treat as a Western convention.
notes: Occasion-matching colour rule with high-authority source.

rule_text: For traditional professional job interviews in conservative sectors the outerwear should be a tailored dark wool coat rather than a sport or athleisure jacket so the outer layer signals the same preparation as the interview outfit.
evidence_keywords: interview, tailored coat, wool, dark, professional
source_title: Style Journal
evidence_basis: Editorial guidance consistently recommends tailored dark outerwear for conservative interview contexts.
rule_scope: Applies to conservative professional interviews.
rule_limitations: Creative-industry interviews may allow softer outerwear.

rule_text: For funeral or memorial occasions shoes should be dark closed-toe leather with a matte or low-shine finish as part of an overall subdued and respectful palette.
evidence_keywords: funeral, memorial, dark shoes, closed toe, matte
source_title: Emily Posts Etiquette
source_author_or_org: Emily Post Institute (Peggy Post et al.)
source_url_or_reference: Emily Posts Etiquette (19th edition), William Morrow, 2017
evidence_basis: Emily Post etiquette advises subdued dark clothing including closed-toe leather shoes for funerals.
rule_scope: Applies to funeral and memorial occasions.
rule_limitations: Cultural practices vary; some traditions require specific white or other colour codes.

rule_text: For cocktail dress-code occasions accessories may be slightly bolder than daytime with metallic touches or statement earrings while stopping short of the fully formal jewellery expected at black-tie.
evidence_keywords: cocktail attire, metallic accessory, statement earring, evening
source_title: Vogue
source_reliability_reason: Major fashion publication with recurring dress-code coverage.
evidence_basis: Vogue occasion features distinguish cocktail dressing from both smart casual and full black-tie accessory conventions.
rule_scope: Applies to cocktail-dress-code evening occasions.
rule_limitations: Not appropriate for black-tie or strictly daytime workwear.
